ud2.9:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, at the Eastern Monastery in Migāra’s mother’s mansion.
ud2.9:1.3: Then at that time Migāra’s mother Visākhā was bound up in some matter or other with the Kosalan King Pasenadi,
ud2.9:1.4: (but) the Kosalan King Pasenadi would not conclude it according to (her) desire.
ud2.9:2.1: Then Migāra’s mother Visākhā in the middle of the day went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, she sat down on one side.
ud2.9:2.2: While sat on one side the Fortunate One said this to Migāra’s mother Visākhā:
ud2.9:2.3: “Well now, Visākhā, where have you come from in the middle of the day?”
ud2.9:2.4: o “Here, reverend Sir, I am bound up in some affair or other with the Kosalan King Pasenadi,
ud2.9:2.5: (but) the Kosalan King Pasenadi does not conclude it according to (my) desire.”
ud2.9:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud2.9:4.1: “All that is in another’s power is painful, ~ all that is mastered is pleasing,
ud2.9:4.3: In sharing they suffer hardship, ~ for yokes are difficult to transcend.”
